children: Experian is launching another $500 million buyback and nudging up its fiscal 2027 profitability guidance, which should be well received and offset its revised top-line outlook, Bernstein's Will Kirkness and Filippo Giardini say in a research note. The U.K. credit-reporting company posted solid results for the first half, with organic revenue growth of 7% in the second quarter, the analysts say. Experian tightened its full-year organic growth to between 6% and 7%, from 6% to 8% previously. But it now expects to expand its benchmark earnings before interest and taxes margin by at least 50 basis points, up from about 50 basis points previously. Consensus expectations--which assume organic growth of 6.9% and a margin expansion of 50 basis points to 29%--seem unlikely to change, Bernstein says. Shares rise 2.2%. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)
